extracted.intended_audience: aspiring stage magicians, conjurers, and theatrical performers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, performance-oriented guidance for conceiving, rehearsing, publicizing, and presenting stage-magic/illusion shows (including training assistants, audience management, and logistics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing and speech delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Control volubility; avoid too rapid patter. 'Ce défaut était une trop grande volubilité de parole; mon boniment, récité du ton d’un écolier, perdait considérablement de son effet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speak slowly and calmly: 'plus un récit est fait lentement, moins il semble long à ceux qui l’écoutent.' Slow delivery conveys interest and makes the audience listen attentively; rapid speech signals eagerness to finish and transmits impatience to listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branded giveaways and souvenirs for publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute memorable, branded gifts that recall the performer's name and the show's content instead of generic ephemeral toys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace cheap toys with illustrated comic journals, elegant fans, albums of the séance, rebuses, bouquets, candies — each inscribed 'Souvenirs des soirées fantastiques de Robert‑Houdin' and carrying short poems or details about the acts. These items both entertain and act as word‑of‑mouth advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a themed printed handout / comic journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a small illustrated parody journal to be read during intermission and to promote the show (example: 'LE CAGLIOSTRO, PASSE‑TEMPS DE L’ENTR’ACTE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parody, faux news, inventions, announcements, and short humorous articles to amuse the audience during the entr'acte and to buy the performer extra preparation time; include bits that describe the experiments and compliment the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous innovation of acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Constantly invent and improve new experiments and effects so that the public's admiration is maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work to minimize reliance on luck: 'il est plus difficile d’entretenir l’admiration que de la faire naître' and 'La vogue d’un artiste ne peut être durable qu’autant que son talent s’accroît chaque jour.' Keep inventing and perfecting new material (e.g., the 'seconde vue').

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive rehearsal and private testing before public debut
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly prepare and test a new effect with exhaustive rehearsals and a variety of combinations before announcing or debuting it publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two months of relentless construction and practice preceded the public presentation of the 'seconde vue'; first public attempt may fail, but careful rehearsal and repeated trials lead to reliable success. Do not present novel, untested methods to a large audience without prior, rigorous trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training observational and rapid-cognition skills for assistants
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop assistants' instantaneous perceptual and memory skills through daily exercises (e.g., rapid addition of dominoes, listing objects seen at a glance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: asking a child to name domino totals immediately (progressing from two to 12 dominoes), practicing passing quickly before shops and later listing many items (the son could list ~40 items). Such exercises form the practical basis for 'second sight' illusions and covert information transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate dual attention / mental multitasking
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice thinking simultaneously about what you say (patter) and what you do (mechanics) to enable improvisation and concealment during performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author learned to 'poursuivre simultanément deux idées' — e.g., inventing new tricks mid‑performance or solving mechanical problems while conversing — which is highly favorable to sleight‑of‑hand and improvisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage casting and presentation to enhance credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose and present assistants (appearance, demeanor) so their look reinforces the intended illusion (e.g., a pale, serious child for a 'miraculous' second sight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The physical bearing of an assistant can strongly influence audience belief; the son's intelligent, serious, pale visage helped create a supernatural impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and plan for skeptical interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect audience attempts to foil or expose an effect and design procedures and contingencies to counter them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready with prepared responses or alternate routings for tricks when challengers attempt to create impossibilities (example: a spectator covering seat numbers to try to break 'seconde vue'); anticipate how skeptics will test the effect and build resilient protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience management during arrivals, intermissions, and impatience
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage crowd expectations and impatience (timing of you vs. curtain, entr'acte length) to avoid public annoyance and to buy prep time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work the pacing of the session, use giveaways and the entr'acte journal to occupy the audience, and when running late at another engagement have contingency actions (e.g., send on an assistant to start) to defuse impatience and turn a bad entrance into a sympathetic moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time management and gatekeeping to protect working time
rubrics_metrics.description: Screen and limit visitors and interruptions using procedural systems so the artist's creative time is preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical system described: an electrical communication to the workshop to transmit visitor's name, acoustic instrument to hear the answer, a button to indicate 'absent' (signal in vestibule) and a hidden touch that rings the servant's bell to create an excuse and move the visitor elsewhere. These devices save significant working time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to abridge unwelcome visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Have planned, polite theatrical devices to shorten or terminate intrusive visits without open rudeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: press a hidden electrical touch while conversing to have the servant stage an interruption and move the visitor to another room, leading most importuns to leave. Use small staged comedies to avoid wasting time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling disturbed or potentially dangerous visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use calm, staged compliance and humane measures when confronted by emotionally disturbed people rather than physical confrontation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: when a veiled, mentally disturbed woman threatened the author, he feigned compliance (performed a fake ritual), defused her panic, returned her money, and then investigated her background and informed family—de‑escalation and aftercare are advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit popularity commercially and socially while it lasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize promptly on public vogue to build fortune as well as fame, because public favor is fleeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept engagements in salons and theatres, monetize souvenirs and publicity, and leverage press attention; be pragmatic about combining financial gain with artistic reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics and contingency planning for multiple engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan travel, timing, and stage logistics precisely when juggling many evening commitments and prepare contingency actions for stage timing mishaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: precise timing between acts, rapid carriage travel, instructing an assistant/child to begin the act if you're delayed, and rehearsing rapid stage entrances to avoid public ire.
